title: [question] Difference of pytorch_quantization modules and torch.ao.quantization
body:
What is relation of pytorch_quantization (if I understand it's a "fake quantization" toolkit for QAT and export to ONNX for TensorRT consumption) and of PyTorch core fake quantization modules in https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/quantization-support.html ?

Is it that pytorch_quantization focuses on "fake quantization" modules and that https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/quantization-support.html#module-torch.ao.nn.qat has only a few fake quantized modules out of the box? (If I understand well, it's https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.ao.quantization.quantize_fx.prepare_qat_fx.html that inserts the fake quantization modules)

Thank you!

comments.author: lix19937
comments.body:
I think, NV PyTorch-Quantization toolkit just for training and evaluating PyTorch models with simulated quantization. Q-DQ node(layer) can be added to the model automatically/ manually, allowing the model to be fine-tuned for accuracy and performance. Quantization is compatible with **NVIDIA int8 kernels** and TRT.    

There are some differences in the details of the quantification methods used between pytorch-quantize-fx with nv-PyTorch-Quantization.

comments.author: zerollzeng
comments.body: @ttyio for viz.

comments.author: vadimkantorov
comments.body:
Because quantization is characterized by many different regimes (hard to grasp as a quantization novice):
- eager vs graph
- static vs dynamic
- ptq vs qat
- fake vs real

I would say it's important to clearly explain in docs/github which modes is nv-pytorch-quantization for and how it's currently different from torch.ao.quantization

comments.author: ttyio
comments.body:
Hi @vadimkantorov , we recommend nv-pytorch-quantization if you are going to deploy using TensorRT.
Here is more links for reference , the whitepaper: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.09602
Also we have a GTC session in https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/on-demand/session/gtcspring21-s31653/

comments.author: vadimkantorov
comments.body: Thanks, so as I understood, it's for QAT training with Fake Quantization in kind of graph/module mode (with operations done in float), targeted for further conversion and deployment with TensorRT (with int8 ops). Correct? So maybe some simple paragraph along these lines in README would clarify situation for novices :) Thanks!

comments.author: ttyio
comments.body: @vadimkantorov thank you for the suggestion. Yes we use fake quant, not only support QAT fine-tuning, we also support PTQ calibration.  There is a link to https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/tensorrt/pytorch-quantization-toolkit/docs/ in the README, and we have document it in the link. we also mention some further optimization topic for TensorRT inference in this doc. Hope this is helpful, thanks again!

comments.author: vadimkantorov
comments.body:
@ttyio 

https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT/blob/46253b644142a1d9632ba463422abfc5dcefc371/tools/pytorch-quantization/pytorch_quantization/nn/modules/tensor_quantizer.py#L312:

```python
if inputs.dtype == torch.half or amax.dtype == torch.half:
    raise Exception("Exporting to ONNX in fp16 is not supported. Please export in fp32, i.e. disable AMP.")
outputs = self._fb_fake_quant(inputs, amax)
```

It seems that this code has not changed since 2021. Is it still correct? I would think that standard PyTorch FakeQuant modules should now be supporting fp16, no?

cc @jerryzh168 @char-nvidia

comments.author: ttyio
comments.body: @vadimkantorov we will remove this in the next release which including the bfloat support. thanks!

comments.author: vadimkantorov
comments.body:
We simply removed this `if`, export passed fine, but then trtexec complains with assert failure that scale is 0 or non-positive.

In the meanwhile, any hints of possible workarounds until the next release? How is it possible for scale variable get to zero? Maybe if the scale is computed in fp16, some underflow?

comments.author: vadimkantorov
comments.body: Overall, it would be good to have an explainer about the role of pytorch_quantization in the modern PyTorch story. pytorch_quantization was conceived 3 years ago, PyTorch's built-in quantization API has improved since then...

comments.author: vadimkantorov
ttyio
comments.body:
@vadimkantorov , yes, for the underflow/overflow issue, yes need more changes, the `amax` should cast to float buffer if low precision detected here: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT/blob/release/8.6/tools/pytorch-quantization/pytorch_quantization/nn/modules/tensor_quantizer.py#L277


for the role of nv pytorch qat tool vs. native pytorch qat, if you check the output onnx, the q/dq placement is different, and trt explicit precision network performance heavily depends on q/dq placement. https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/tensorrt/developer-guide/index.html#qdq-placement-recs

comments.author: ttyio
comments.body: @vadimkantorov btw, I see your code point to qat tool `2.1.2`, if you check the latest `release/8.6` branch, you will see latest qat `2.1.3` version.

comments.author: vadimkantorov
comments.body:
@ttyio No, the same code in release/8.6: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT/blob/release/8.6/tools/pytorch-quantization/pytorch_quantization/nn/modules/tensor_quantizer.py#L279-L314 :(

It would be great to including screenshots with such Q-DQ examples and differences into docs!

comments.author: vadimkantorov
comments.body:
> @ttyio Maybe if the scale is computed in fp16, some underflow?
> 
> Then it should just replace to `amax_sequeeze.to(torch.float32) / bound.to(torch.float32)`
> 
> Also, there is a typo, `amax_sequeeze` should likely be `amax_squeeze`

@ttyio btw this seems to make export work: `amax_sequeeze.to(torch.float32) / float(bound)`

But still somehow the output of the gemm is float32 when looking at the ONNX graph. How can I force it to be float16? (all inputs and the nn.Linear were converted to torch.float16 prior to export)

comments.author: ttyio
vadimkantorov
comments.body:
In general, what was the basis for those constraints against fp16? If we still want to do it, do we just need to patch the onnx file?

(Or is the next release supporting fp16/opset19 just around the corner?)

In our very simple case, the fp16 kernel was allowed, but there still was inserted a reformat node to convert back to fp32 output. So it affects benchmark faithfulness and may even affect the selected kernels?

comments.author: ttyio
comments.body:
> but there still was inserted a reformat node to convert back from fp32 output.

 @vadimkantorov , this is not caused by fp16/opset19, TRT is weak typed till version 8.6. Is this layer mark as network output? or the next layer run in FP32?

comments.author: vadimkantorov
comments.body: As network output. We'll create a separate issue with more details...

comments.author: ttyio
comments.body: @vadimkantorov  network out is FP32 by default, to remove the reformat, change the network output to Fp16 follow this sample: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT/tree/release/8.6/samples/sampleIOFormats
